processing: Ripe pu-erh from the Menghai Tea Factory: wet-piled sun-dried Yunnan large-leaf tea, blended to a numbered recipe and pressed.
harvest_season: Not tied to one picking: factory recipes are blended from stored material.
appearance_dry: Pressed ripe tea in brown tones; the usual format of this recipe is not well documented.
appearance_liquor: Dark red-brown, as usual for Menghai ripe pu-erh.
appearance_wet: Soft dark brown leaf, as usual for ripe pu-erh.
taste_profile: Little tasting detail is recorded for this recipe; expect what is typical of Menghai ripe tea, with earth, dark sweetness and a smooth body.

brewing.notes: Standard ripe handling: rinse once and use near-boiling water.

vintage_note: Dayi teas are normally sold by year and batch, with a code such as 1801 meaning the first batch of 2018. One catalogue records seven ripe productions under 0532, plus one raw, so this is a recurring but minor recipe. Check the wrapper to see whether a given example is ripe.
description:
0532 is one of the numbered recipes of the Menghai Tea Factory, the maker behind the Dayi brand. It is a minor one: you are far more likely to meet its siblings 7572 or 7262.

As a ripe tea it is piled and fermented before pressing. Informal explanations of Menghai numbers treat the first two digits as the year of the recipe, the third as the main leaf grade and the last, 2, as the Menghai factory. On that reading 0532 would be a 2005 recipe built around grade 3 leaf, but this is an inference, not a factory statement.

There is not much on record about how it tastes. Expect the usual Menghai ripe profile, and brew it hot after a rinse.

Catalogue records show the number on both ripe and raw productions, so read the wrapper. Note the batch code too, since it tells you the production year.
history:
The Menghai Tea Factory dates to 1940, took its present name in 1953 and was among the first two factories making ripe pu-erh in 1973. It became fully private in 1996 and adopted the Dayi trademark.

Little is documented about 0532 itself: neither its creation date nor its blend has been published in any detail. One catalogue lists seven ripe productions and one raw under the number.
